name: tw-sugarcube-ts-tools
description: Editor intelligence for SugarCube in TypeScript/JavaScript: real types on hover, parameter and return-type checking, completion, and go-to-definition for members of setup, State.variables, State.temporary, and settings.

twSugarcube.passageLinks.markdownDescription: Make `setup`/variable members in passages ctrl+clickable by registering them as document links. Only needed as a workaround: Twee 3 Language Tools <= 0.34.0 has a definition provider that never resolves, which blocks native ctrl+click for every extension. VS Code always underlines document links, so leave this off unless you need the gesture.

twSugarcube.strict.markdownDescription: Type the members of `setup`, `State.variables`, `State.temporary`, and `settings` from their assignments, so wrong arguments, wrong types, and typos are reported. Turn this off to keep those containers permissive (`any`) — useful if a story assigns members in ways the plugin can't see.

twSugarcube.passageGoToDefinition.markdownDescription: Bind F12 in passage files to this extension's own go-to-definition, bypassing VS Code's definition aggregation. Only needed as a workaround for the same Twee 3 Language Tools hang. It resolves `setup`/variable members by scanning the workspace, and does NOT know about macros or widgets — so with a fixed Twee 3 Language Tools, the built-in F12 is strictly better.

twSugarcube.typoDetection.markdownDescription: Report members that were never assigned anywhere as errors, so `setup.attck` is caught instead of silently typed `any`. Requires `#twSugarcube.strict#`. Only turn this on if your story creates `setup` and variable members by plain assignment in TypeScript or `<<set>>`: anything created another way — `Object.assign`, a computed `setup[name] =`, or a `.js` file outside the TypeScript project — will be reported as a typo. `settings` is never closed, because SugarCube's Setting API creates those members.

scripts.test: npm run bundle && node test/twee-projection.mjs && node test/passages-transport.mjs && node test/tsserver-smoke.mjs && node test/lint-cli.mjs
scripts.package: npm run bundle && npm test && vsce package
